conj:wedderburn-bratteli-recursion:
Conjecture Wedderburn--Bratteli recursion for Jones--Markov weights y_\lambda at H_n(R, q). At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the Jones–Markov weight of every shape with three or more rows is 0, and on the two-row shape (a, b), a \geq b, it is

  y_{(a,b)}
  \;=\;
  \frac{[a - b + 1]_q}{[2]_q^{\,a+b}},

with [k]_q the balanced q-integer. These weights satisfy a Bratteli recursion in two equivalent forms.

Restriction (sum over the Bratteli edges out of (a, b)):

  y_{(a,b)}
  \;=\;
  y_{(a+1,\,b)} \;+\; y_{(a,\,b+1)}.

When a = b the second shape is not a partition, and the formula assigns it weight [0]_q = 0.

Single edge. With d = a - b + 1, adding a cell to the first or second row gives

  y_{(a+1,\,b)}
  \;=\;
  \frac{[d+1]_q}{[2]_q\,[d]_q}\; y_{(a,b)},
  \qquad
  y_{(a,\,b+1)}
  \;=\;
  \frac{[d-1]_q}{[2]_q\,[d]_q}\; y_{(a,b)}.

So the per-edge factor is F_q = [d \pm 1]_q / ([2]_q [d]_q), depending on which row receives the cell. Each single edge determines y_\lambda^{(n+1)} from one parent; summing these factors over all parents of \lambda would double-count.

Derivation. The closed form is the Markov-trace weight, not a postulate: y_{(a,b)} equals the Ocneanu weight w_{(a,b)}(z) at z = q^3/(q^2+1), the weight of the unique Markov trace on the Hecke tower at that parameter. On two rows the hook-content product telescopes to q^{2b}(1 + q^2 + \cdots + q^{2(a-b)})/(q^2+1)^{a+b}, which is [a-b+1]_q/[2]_q^{a+b}. Every shape with three or more rows has weight 0 there, so the trace factors through the Temperley–Lieb quotient.

This recursion confirms that \alpha_k(H_n) at a fixed k involves only finitely many strata. The tower of Jones-Markov weights propagates without requiring expensive p(n) \times p(n) linear-system solves.
rem:wedderburn-bratteli-recursion-proof-:
Remark Proof sketch: wedderburn bratteli recursion.

Proof

Write t = [2]_q = q + q^{-1} and d = a - b + 1. The balanced q-integers satisfy

  [d+1]_q + [d-1]_q \;=\; t\,[d]_q,

since (q^{d+1} - q^{-d-1}) + (q^{d-1} - q^{1-d}) = (q + q^{-1})(q^d - q^{-d}).

Restriction. y_{(a+1,b)} + y_{(a,b+1)} = \bigl([d+1]_q + [d-1]_q\bigr)/t^{a+b+1} = t\,[d]_q / t^{a+b+1} = y_{(a,b)}.

Single edge. Adding a cell to the first row raises a - b by one and the total by one, so t\,[d]_q\, y_{(a+1,b)} = [d+1]_q\,[d]_q / t^{a+b} = [d+1]_q\, y_{(a,b)}. The second row is the same with [d-1]_q.

Three-row shapes carry weight 0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1), so the recursion on two-row shapes is the whole recursion. The divisions are by [2]_q and [d]_q, non-zero at generic q. At n = 3 the weights are ([4]_q/[2]_q^3,\; 1/[2]_q^2,\; 0). \square

The normalisation \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} f^\lambda y_\lambda = 1 follows by induction on n from the restriction identity together with the Young branching rule f^\lambda = \sum_{\mu \nearrow \lambda} f^\mu.

    y_\lambda \cdot \chi_\lambda(r_k),

Pre-Archimedean Derivation Chain: Step-by-Step.

A particle mass is derived from the categorical action of a quantum observable universe. The algorithm behind each step follows. Every intermediate quantity belongs to \mathbb{Q}(q). No analytic limits or empirical constants enter until the final Archimedean specialisation.

Three weak-sector inputs calibrate the framework: the electron mass m_e fixes the unit, the neutron beta-sector bar-skew channel fixes q_0, and the pion mass fixes the orthogonal meson scale. All other observables—nucleon masses, binding energies, decay Q-values—are derived algebraically at q_0.

Steps 1–8 construct the categorical trace inside the Iwahori–Hecke algebra. Steps 9–11 extract physical values.

Step 1: The categorical action A quantum observable universe provides a braided category \mathbf{C} acting on a state bundle. This categorical action yields a braid group representation \rho_n where the R-matrix generates the strand crossings. This representation drives all subsequent computations.

Step 2: Holonomy to Hecke relation Yekutieli's surface integration maps the braided category to an Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q). The R-matrix parallel transport ensures flatness, yielding the Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1. The eigenvalue split into \cosh(\ln q) and \sinh(\ln q) separates binding from decay.

Step 3: Knots and the unique trace Every hadron corresponds to a knot closure. Jones’s uniqueness theorem guarantees a single Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M captures the knot invariant unambiguously. Mass, binding, and decay are evaluations of this one algebraic functional.

Step 4: Operator selection The genus-four state space admits exactly six independent crossing operators. The H_3(q) basis in Gröbner–Shirshov normal form supplies them. The Wedderburn summands indexing the mass formula mirror the curve's automorphism Prym decomposition.

Step 5: Wedderburn blocks Semisimplicity splits H_n(q) into Wedderburn matrix blocks indexed by partitions. This renders the trace a finite sum. Hoefsmit seminormal representations compute the matrix traces. The Wenzl branching rule provides the central weights y_\lambda(q). The full invariant factors block-by-block.

Step 6: The Frobenius integral and chirality The Markov trace is the Frobenius integral on the symmetric algebra H_n(q). The absolute trace evaluates the absolute categorical mass. The Kauffman framing formula supplies the ribbon twist, matching the knot's chirality to its phase.

Step 7: Normal forms and finite slices The Gröbner–Shirshov basis algorithms rewrite braid words to their canonical normal forms. The associated spectral sequence collapses at E_2. Computations therefore require only finite jet-order slices, avoiding infinite-series divergence.

Step 8: Jet order The slice-traversal matches the jet order. Convergence confirms the finite-slice evaluation remains algebraically consistent with the expected semiclassical limit at q \to 1.

Step 9: Mass evaluation The Archimedean realisation evaluates the rational trace at q_0 and multiplies by the electron scale. This converts the symbolic invariant into a physical mass. The real part of the categorical volume computes the binding energy, while the imaginary part determines the decay Q-value.

Step 10: Canonical knot identification A semidefinite program selects the canonical Hecke element. Minimizing the Frobenius residual over Gröbner–Shirshov normal forms identifies the ground state. The dual shadow prices explicitly recover the binding energy block saturation.

      & K \text{ torus} \\[4pt]
    0 & K \text{ unknot}
  \end{cases}

routes the physical weight of a state through its fundamental topological geometry. Each of the three cases arises from an established theorem in low-dimensional topology.

1. The piecewise split: Thurston's Geometrization. Thurston's theorem for knot complements states that S^3 \setminus K admits exactly one of three geometric structures: (i) a hyperbolic metric of constant negative curvature (the vast majority of knots), (ii) a Seifert-fibred structure (torus knots, Vol = 0), or (iii) a decomposition along tori into simpler pieces (satellite knots). The piecewise definition of \mathrm{Geom}(K) follows this classification directly.

2. The hyperbolic case: the Volume Conjecture. For hyperbolic K, \mathrm{Geom}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2. This originates from the Kashaev--Murakami--Murakami Volume Conjecture: the asymptotic growth of the coloured Jones polynomial J_K^{(n)}(q) at roots of unity is dominated by \mathrm{Vol}(K). In the categorical framework, c_K = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\mathcal{B}_K)) is the Hecke algebra Frobenius character of the braid \mathcal{B}_K, and its leading asymptotics recover \mathrm{Vol}(K). Division by \hbar_q^2 = (1 - 1/q)^2 maps the topological volume to a mass/energy scale.

3. The torus case: Chern--Simons dominance. For torus knots K = T_{m,n}, the hyperbolic volume vanishes. The topological weight is purely the phase of the path integral, which is the Chern--Simons invariant

  \mathrm{CS}(T_{m,n})
  = \frac{\pi^2(m^2-1)(n^2-1)}{12mn}.

Multiplying by \hbar_q^2 (rather than dividing) establishes a strict duality between hyperbolic and torus states: if hyperbolic knots represent massive, localised "bulk" particles where \hbar_q^2 suppresses the volume, torus knots represent boundary/phase states where \hbar_q^2 amplifies the Chern--Simons phase.

4. Self-duality and the Frobenius pairing. The \mathrm{Vol}/\hbar_q^2 vs \mathrm{CS} \cdot \hbar_q^2 duality is the Frobenius pairing of the knot with its dual in the Hecke algebra. For a hyperbolic knot K, the dual K^* (mirror image) satisfies \mathrm{Vol}(K^*) = \mathrm{Vol}(K) and the Frobenius inner product \langle K, K^* \rangle = 1 (via the Markov trace). The factor \hbar_q^2 mediates this pairing:

  \langle K, K^* \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}}
  = \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^2}
    \cdot \frac{\hbar_q^2}{\mathrm{Vol}(K^*)}
  = 1.

For torus knots (which are self-dual under the descent involution), the pairing goes through the CS functional, and \hbar_q^2 appears multiplicatively because the torus knot's phase is the pairing.

The figure-eight knot 4_1 is special: it is amphicheiral (K = K^*), so the self-pairing is manifestly real. This underlies the figure-eight BW modification factors 1 - h^2 and h[2]_q (figure-eight BW coefficients), both of which are real algebraic expressions in q.

5. The unknot: vacuum normalisation. The unknot bounds a disk; its complement has trivial geometry (\mathrm{Vol} = 0, \mathrm{CS} = 0). Setting \mathrm{Geom}(\bigcirc) = 0 ensures that unknotted loops do not contribute spurious mass or energy to the categorical trace.
prf:frobenius-codim-universal:
Proof Proof of frobenius codim universal. Since p_\lambda is central and primitive in Z(A), and each p_\lambda is \tau-dual to itself up to the scalar \tau(p_\lambda), linearity of \tau gives

  \tau(C_{\dim_q})
  \;=\;
  \sum_\lambda \frac{1}{\dim_q(\lambda) \cdot \tau(p_\lambda)}
    \cdot \tau(p_\lambda)
  \;=\;
  \sum_\lambda \frac{1}{\dim_q(\lambda)}.

\square

C_{\dim_q} is not forced by its trace. The element C_{\dim_q} is not the unique central element with trace \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda) whenever A has at least two blocks: \tau is a single linear functional on Z(A), which has dimension |\widehat{A}| = p(n) \geq 2 for n \geq 2, so every z = \sum_\lambda c_\lambda p_\lambda with \sum_\lambda c_\lambda\,\tau(p_\lambda) = \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda) has the same trace. The coefficients c_\lambda = 1/(\dim_q(\lambda)\,\tau(p_\lambda)) are a block-by-block definition, not forced by the trace.

C_{\dim_q} is categorical in three distinct senses:

  1. The Frobenius pairing \tau \colon A \otimes A \to \mathbb{C} is a morphism in the monoidal category of A-bimodules; C_{\dim_q} is built from it by universal constructions (central idempotents + duality).
  2. The q-dimension \dim_q(\lambda) is the categorical quantum trace of the identity on the simple module V_\lambda — intrinsic to a ribbon-category / rigid-monoidal structure.
  3. In the equivalence between Frobenius algebras and 2D TQFTs (Atiyah–Segal / Abrams 1996 / Kock 2004 §2), every element of A corresponds to a decorated 2-cobordism. The standard Casimir \Omega = \sum e_i \cdot e^i corresponds to the torus with puncture; C_{\dim_q} corresponds to the torus with a \dim_q-labelled puncture, i.e., the torus twisted by the ribbon-category structure.

TQFT / handle-element interpretation. For a 2-dimensional TQFT with state-space A, the handle element of the torus-with-one-puncture is \mathrm{HE}_A := \sum_\lambda p_\lambda / \tau(p_\lambda) and its trace \tau(\mathrm{HE}_A) = \sum_\lambda d_\lambda (classical-dimension sum, e.g., the number of involutions for A = H_n(R, q)). The element C_{\dim_q} is the quantum refinement of the handle: an additional factor 1/\dim_q(\lambda) per block rescales by the block's quantum dimension rather than its classical one.

In Reshetikhin–Turaev language: if the MTC associated with A has S-matrix S_{\lambda\mu}, then \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = S_{\mathbf{1}, \mathbf{0}}^{-1} \cdot \sum_\lambda \dim_q(\lambda)^{-1} (modulo normalisation), which is a reciprocal of the global dimension weighted by self-duality.

Specialisations.

  1. A = H_n(R, q) with Markov trace \tau = \mathrm{tr}_M, \dim_q = q-hook-length dimension. \widehat{A} = \{\lambda \vdash n\}. Then \mathrm{tr}_M(C_{\dim_q}) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} 1/\dim_q(\lambda). At n = 3: = 2 + 1/[2]_q.
  2. A = Temperley–Lieb \mathrm{TL}_n(q) with Markov trace. \widehat{A} = \{\text{Jones–Wenzl idempotents}\}. The co-Casimir trace is a q-weighted sum over Jones–Wenzl blocks.
  3. A = group algebra \mathbb{C}[G] with \tau = uniform (Haar) trace. \dim_q = \dim (classical). Then \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = \sum_\lambda 1/\dim(\lambda), the reciprocal-dimension character sum — a known group-theoretic invariant related to the number of conjugacy classes via the first-orthogonality identity.

GB-filtration (confinement) decomposition. When A = H_n(R, q) is filtered by the confinement filtration J^\bullet(q) (confinement level), the partitions \lambda sort by level \ell(\lambda) = \mathrm{height}(\lambda) - 1. The Frobenius co-Casimir trace decomposes

  \tau(C_{\dim_q})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\ell = 0}^{n-1} \;
    \sum_{\lambda :\; \ell(\lambda) = \ell}
      \frac{1}{\dim_q(\lambda)},

with the self-dual pairing under Young-diagram transpose (\lambda \leftrightarrow \lambda') identifying level \ell with level n - 1 - \ell. Each self-dual pair contributes an equal 1/\dim_q value (since \dim_q(\lambda) = \dim_q(\lambda') for any q). At the extremes \ell = 0 and \ell = n-1:

  \dim_q\bigl((n)\bigr) \;=\; 1 \;=\; \dim_q\bigl((1^n)\bigr),

so, when both blocks are included, levels 0 and n-1 contribute exactly 1 each, giving the bound

  \tau(C_{\dim_q}) \;\geq\; 2 \qquad \text{for all } n \geq 1.

Middle levels carry all the q-dependence. For n = 3 only one middle level exists (level 1, \lambda = (2,1)), giving \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = 2 + 1/[2]_q when every block is included. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the block (1^n) has \tau(p_{(1^n)}) = 0 for n \geq 3 and must be dropped, so the bound \geq 2 does not hold there; at n = 3 the sum over \widehat{A}^{\circ} = \{(3), (2,1)\} is 1 + 1/[2]_q.

Independence of the vortex \varrho. \tau(C_{\dim_q}^{(A)}) is independent of the specific vortex \varrho — it depends only on the algebra A (equivalently on n and q), not on the braid word \sigma_w representing \varrho. This is both a feature and a limitation:

  • Feature (universality): Every vortex on H_3(R, q) — proton (uud), neutron (udd), any nucleon-like trefoil — inherits the same additive offset, (2 + 1/[2]_q) \cdot m_e with every block included (not available at z = q^3/(q^2+1), see above). Mass differences between nucleons come entirely from the descended |\mathrm{tr}_M| and brane-tower pieces, not from the Frobenius correction.
  • Limitation (vortex-blind): The Frobenius correction cannot by itself distinguish \varrho_{\mathfrak{p}} from \varrho_{\mathfrak{n}} or any other trefoil-like vortex. Vortex-dependent corrections — e.g. chirality factors \{1+h, 1-h^2, (1-h^2)^2\} per (figure-eight BW coefficients) or knot-factor Frobenius pairings per (knot-factor Frobenius pairing) — are separate structural terms beyond \tau(C_{\dim_q}).

The unified mass formula (unified knot mass) therefore has three tiers:

  1. Vortex-specific: descended |\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_w)| and brane tower \sum \Phi_q.
  2. Algebra-specific (but vortex-independent): Frobenius co-Casimir \tau(C_{\dim_q}^{(A)}).
  3. Isotope-specific (vortex-dependent but structural): chirality / knot-factor coefficients from the six-term mass formula.

Consistency.

  1. At q = 1 (classical limit): \dim_q \to d_\lambda and \tau(p_\lambda) \to d_\lambda^2/|G| (normalised group-algebra trace), so C_{\dim_q} reduces to \sum_\lambda |G|/d_\lambda^3 \cdot p_\lambda and its trace is \sum_\lambda 1/d_\lambda — the classical reciprocal-dimension sum.
  2. In the "single-vortex" case A = H_3(R, q), three blocks \{(3), (2,1), (1,1,1)\} with q-dims \{1, [2]_q, 1\} give \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = 2 + 1/[2]_q when all three blocks are included. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), \tau(p_{(1,1,1)}) = 0, so the (1,1,1) term is undefined and the sum over the surviving blocks is 1 + 1/[2]_q.
  3. The self-duality \lambda \leftrightarrow \lambda' is the categorical shadow of the Young-diagram transpose symmetry of the Hecke algebra, which in turn descends from the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1}) \sigma_i + 1 admitting two eigenvalues (q, -q^{-1}) — the source of all q-deformation structure in the paper.

The convention used throughout is the quantum hook-length formula \dim_q(\lambda) = [n]_q!\,/\,\prod_{x \in \lambda} [h_x]_q, which reduces to the classical S_n-irrep dimension at q = 1.

prop:content-scaling-correspondence:
Proposition Box content is the q-Jucys--Murphy eigenvalue exponent. Under q-Schur--Weyl duality [jimbo1986] V^{\otimes n} \cong \bigoplus_\lambda V_\lambda \otimes S_\lambda, let T be a standard tableau of shape \lambda \vdash n and let c = j - i be the content of the box of T at position (i,j) holding the value k. Proposition Frobenius Casimir of H_3(q): Schur elements, Markov weights, its Markov trace, and \sum_{\lambda\vdash3}1/\dim_q\lambda = 2+1/[2]_q. Let K be a field and q\in K^\times with q^2+1\ne0 and q^4+q^2+1\ne0. Let H_3=H_3(K,q) have generators \sigma_1,\sigma_2 with \sigma_i^2=(q-q^{-1})\sigma_i+1 and standard basis \{T_w\}_{w\in S_3}. Write h=q-q^{-1}, [2]_q=q+q^{-1}, and let \kappa(\lambda) be the content sum of \lambda. The canonical symmetrising form is \tau_0(T_w)=\delta_{w,1}, with dual basis T_w^\vee=T_{w^{-1}}. Its Frobenius Casimir is C_{\mathrm{Frob}}:=\sum_{w\in S_3}T_wT_{w^{-1}}. For z\in K, \mathrm{tr}^z is the Ocneanu trace (\mathrm{tr}^z(1)=1, \mathrm{tr}^z(x\sigma_2)=z\,\mathrm{tr}^z(x) for x\in H_2), and write z_0 = q^3/(q^2+1) for the two-row Markov parameter. Then:

  1. (Casimir.) C_{\mathrm{Frob}} = 6+3h(T_{s_1}+T_{s_2})+h^2(T_{s_1s_2}+T_{s_2s_1})+(q^3-q^{-3})T_{w_0}. It is central and acts on the block \lambda by c_\lambda d_\lambda, where d_\lambda is the block dimension and the Schur elements of \tau_0 are c_\lambda = q^{\kappa(\lambda)}\prod_{x\in\lambda}[h_x]_q: c_{(3)}=q^3[3]_q!, c_{(2,1)}=[3]_q, c_{(1^3)}=q^{-3}[3]_q!.
  2. (Markov weights.) \mathrm{tr}^z=\sum_\lambda y_\lambda(z)\chi_\lambda with
y_{(3)}=\frac{(qz+1)(q^3z+qz+1)}{(q^2+1)(q^4+q^2+1)},\qquad
y_{(2,1)}=\frac{q(q-z)(qz+1)}{q^4+q^2+1},\qquad
y_{(1^3)}=\frac{q^2(z-q)(q^2z+z-q^3)}{(q^2+1)(q^4+q^2+1)}.

At z = z_0 = q^3/(q^2+1): y_{(3)}=(q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2, y_{(2,1)}=1/[2]_q^2 and y_{(1^3)}=0. 3. (Trace of the Casimir.)

\mathrm{tr}^z(C_{\mathrm{Frob}}) = 6+6hz+2h^2z^2+(q^3-q^{-3})(hz^2+z),

and at z_0 = q^3/(q^2+1)

\mathrm{tr}^{z_0}(C_{\mathrm{Frob}})=\frac{(q^4+q^2+1)(q^6+q^4+q^2+5)}{(q^2+1)^2},
\mathrm{tr}^{z_0}(C_{\mathrm{Frob}})-\Bigl(2+\frac1{[2]_q}\Bigr)=\frac{q^{10}+2q^8+3q^6+5q^4-q^3+2q^2-q+3}{(q^2+1)^2}.

In particular \mathrm{tr}^{z_0}(C_{\mathrm{Frob}})\ne 2+1/[2]_q as rational functions of q (at q=1 the two sides are 6 and 5/2). 4. (Inverse q-dimension sum.) With \dim_q\lambda=[3]_q!/\prod_{x\in\lambda}[h_x]_q,

\sum_{\lambda\vdash 3}\frac{1}{\dim_q\lambda} = \frac{1}{[3]_q!}\sum_{\lambda\vdash3}q^{-\kappa(\lambda)}c_\lambda = 2+\frac{1}{[2]_q},

and over the blocks on which \mathrm{tr}^{z_0} is nonzero the sum is 1+1/[2]_q=(q^2+q+1)/(q^2+1). 5. (The element C_{\dim_q} is not the Frobenius Casimir.) For any trace t on H_3 with t(e_\lambda)\ne0 for all \lambda, the central element C_{\dim_q}=\sum_\lambda e_\lambda/(\dim_q(\lambda)\,t(e_\lambda)) of Universal Frobenius co-dimension trace: \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda) has t(C_{\dim_q})=\sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q\lambda by construction. At z_0 = q^3/(q^2+1) it is undefined, because \mathrm{tr}^{z_0}(e_{(1^3)})=0.

Two inputs are cited rather than proved here: that C_{\mathrm{Frob}} acts on block \lambda by the scalar c_\lambda d_\lambda in item 1, of which only the implied trace identity is established, and the associativity of the six-dimensional matrix model of H_3 used to compute in it.

So the identity \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q\lambda=2+1/[2]_q is a formal sum (item 4), and it is not the Markov trace of the Frobenius Casimir (item 3).
